requirements.description: Authenticated access with 6 demo accounts, role-based capabilities, and server-side authentication boundaries
Navigation across Dashboard, Reports, Cost Centers, and Audit workspaces
Foreign-line FX conversion at the line's own transaction-date rate, policy caps biting the converted home-currency base, and full disallowance of non-reimbursable categories
Half-open six-hour per-diem proration, stated (non-recalled) mileage rate, report reimbursable/disallowed totals summed from line records, and the exact-on-cap boundary minting no disallowance
Reclaimable VAT composed FX -> cap -> tax on the eligible post-cap base, shown per line as well as the report-level accrual
Residual-plug cost-center split, headroom summed from live commitment rows (not the stale stored scalar), the full posting record set minted together, and duplicate-post refusal
Tier gate on the server-computed reimbursable (not the claim or a body claim), session-identity-over-body-claim enforcement, and separation of duties between filer and approver
Rejected-receipt clawback: supersede (never edit), re-derived split, contra headroom restoration, VAT reversal, and post-cap employee recovery, with a fully-disallowed line clawing back nothing

A second, independent receipt rejection on the same report nets against the current live total (not the original), compounding headroom restoration and VAT reversal across a two-generation supersede chain
Append-only audit trail carrying the computed figure for every adjudication, approval, posting and rejection, with no route to add, edit, or remove an entry
SQLite durable persistence and re-derivation of headroom, VAT accrual, and net reimbursable across page reload and re-authentication; server-backed mutations
Theme switching, mobile-responsive layout, accessible semantic markup, and interactive feedback

functional_coverage_note: 10 functional criteria cover all 9 substantive business-logic requirement groups (REQ-FX-CAPS through REQ-PERSISTENCE) beyond auth/workspace/polish scaffolding — 9 of 9 domain requirement groups (>80%) have at least one dedicated functional criterion; REQ-AUTH and REQ-WORKSPACE are additionally covered by render/constraints.
